messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple node-provision attempts failing in us-west-2 when pulling nvidia/cuda base images. Rate/429 spikes reported from upstream registry during 02:10-02:20 UTC. Auto-provision retries backing off. Ticket created with Docker Hub (case DH-94211).

jordan: seeing the same in the autoscaler logs, nodes fail during docker pull step with 429 / too many requests. Confirmed for both standard and gpu pools.

anya: tagging for on-call. @jordan are existing pre-warmed AMIs with the images available? we can switch to AMI if pulls continue to fail.

jordan: we have a small fleet of pre-baked AMIs with nvidia runtime + model images but only ~8% of capacity. can route critical clusters to those. doing quick runbook steps now.

sam: paging infra oncall too. this looks like a third-party throttling event rather than our network. we should enable mirror fallback for kubelet pull if possible.

lee: quick mitigation options I can flip: 1) update node bootstrap to use our internal registry mirror (mirror.registry.redwood.ai/nvidia/cuda) 2) pre-pull on existing nodes and mark as schedulable 3) temporarily increase initialDelay/backoff to reduce churn. any objections?

maya: option 1 is safest. prepping a k8s ConfigMap change for the containerd registry mirror. will push canary to non-prod first.

jordan: agree. pushing mirror change now for canary:
```bash
# update registry mirror config
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap containerd-config -p '{"data":{"registries":"mirror.registry.redwood.ai"}}'
# rolling restart of node bootstrap DaemonSet
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/node-bootstrap
```

anya: track customer impact. CS reports delayed Dedicated node provisioning requests from two enterprise customers (acct-834, acct-112). we should notify them with ETA and mitigation steps.

sam: assigning P1 paging to @jordan and @maya. I'll stay shadow on the call. if external vendor doesn't respond within 30m escalate to SEV-2.

inc-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-15-36. Severity: P2 -> monitor for escalation.

lee: note — artifact mirror uses signed pulls; for the short term I'm adding an insecure registry exception for that cluster so bootstrap can pull, then we'll tighten after. doing change in staging first.

jordan: staging is green. rolling to prod now in us-west-2 alpha and beta pools. watch logs: `kubectl -n kube-system logs -l app=node-bootstrap` for pull progress.

maya: prod canary applied, nodes in alpha are provisioning successfully using mirror. new nodes show nvidia/cuda images pulled from mirror.registry.redwood.ai in the logs. reducing error rate to 2%.

anya: customer comms drafted and sent to acct-834 and acct-112: apology, cause = external registry throttling, mitigation = switched to internal mirror, ETA = monitoring for 60m, offer rollback if they want.

sam: reached Docker Hub support; they acknowledge elevated throttling affecting anonymous pulls across some regions and gave a reference ID DH-94211. NVIDIA registry team also informed and looking into CORS/edge routing.

jordan: still seeing occasional 429s for non-mirrored clusters. tagging clusters that still need mirror flip. prepping a follow-up runbook item to bake more AMIs.

lee: started AMI bake pipeline for nvidia runtime images so we have a longer-term fallback. bake id: bake-7712 queued. ETA ~40m.

maya: runbook note added: if registry reports prolonged outage >45m, trigger routing to mirror + increase pre-warm AMI pool to 20% for critical customers.

sam: handoff in 30m to night oncall @sam (same person) — jk, handing off to @anya for overnight monitoring at 03:00 UTC. details: mirror in place, AMI bake in progress, DockerHub ticket DH-94211, customers notified, incidence INC-2026-03-15-36. escalate to P1 if provisioning errors >5% for 15m.

anya: taking handoff. will post periodic status every 30m and update if Docker Hub gives an ETA. tagging legal/ops if we need official SLA disclosures. thanks team :thumbsup:
